sections.content: How many people are "retail cashiers and check-out operators"?

81,935 people

were counted on the census as "retail cashiers and check-out operators" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Retail cashiers and check-out operators accept payments from customers and give change in respect of sales or services.

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "retail cashiers and check-out operators" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 20 to 24 years. Of the whole working population 7.9% were aged 20 to 24 years. For people working as "retail cashiers and check-out operators", 14.2% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "retail cashiers and check-out operators" was 40 to 44 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "retail cashiers and check-out operators" included:

  • farm workers
  • shelf fillers
  • elementary administration occupations (other)

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "retail cashiers and check-out operators" there were more women than men (72.7% compared with 27.3%).

This means "retail cashiers and check-out operators" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "sales occupations".

Men made up 27.3% and women made up 72.7% of "retail cashiers and check-out operators"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "retail cashiers and check-out operators" included:

  • medical radiographers
  • physiotherapists
  • cleaning and housekeeping managers and supervisors

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "retail cashiers and check-out operators" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of women with this occupation than men.

The percentage of men and women who are "retail cashiers and check-out operators" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "retail cashiers and check-out operators", 15.9% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work part-time than full-time (79.3% compared with 20.7%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (98.7%) than self-employed (1.3%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
